item.title: Todd Monken: Week 1 was tough, our guys trusted the process
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Browns moved to 3-1 when Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers's final, desperate heave was picked off by safety Grant Delpit on Thursday night and head coach Todd Monken reflected on how improbable that record would have felt not so long ago.
item.content:encoded:
The Browns moved to 3-1 when Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers's final, desperate heave was picked off by safety Grant Delpit on Thursday night and head coach Todd Monken reflected on how improbable that record would have felt not so long ago.

Week 1 saw the Jaguars pummel Monken's team in his head coaching debut and much of the conversation was about whether they would bench quarterback Deshaun Watson before their Week 3 home opener. Those discussions all centered around the incessant boos Watson heard from Browns fans in an August preseason game against the Bills, but it turned out to be a lot of wasted words.

Watson has led game-winning drives in the fourth quarter each of the last three weeks and the entire Browns team has had little resemblance to the one that got blown out in Jacksonville.

"It’s a credit, I’ll go back to Deshaun, but to our team. I mean, that was a complete, maybe disaster is a little bit strong, but that’s a tough opening game in every phase, other than maybe kickoff return, maybe, other than that," Monken said, via a transcript from the team. "But the guys trusted the process. We got stung a little bit, and our guys responded to that. And, man, that locker room is fun, right there celebrating those guys. Big, big, big divisional win. And so, but Deshaun, before the game, I got a chance to, I was in the coach’s office, and I was going over the call sheet with him again, and I said, 'Isn’t this really cool? Like, you’re going to be introduced last, isn’t that really freaking cool?' It was only seven weeks earlier, and, right, it’s, 'Where are we going to go from here, right? The Bills game at home, right? Where are we going from here, where are you going, where are we going?' So cool."

Monken noted later in his press conference that its only three wins and there is certainly a lot of football left to be played, but that's a promising prospect for Cleveland rather than a distressing one for the first time in a long time.

item.title: Travis Kelce set to surpass Tim Brown, move into No. 7 on NFL's all-time receptions list
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's next catch will be a significant one for his place in NFL history.
item.content:encoded:
Chiefs tight end Travis Kelce's next catch will be a significant one for his place in NFL history.

Kelce has 1,094 receptions in his NFL career, tying him with Tim Brown on the all-time list. With his next catch, Kelce will move ahead of Brown and be No. 7 in NFL history for career catches.

In first place on the all-time catch list is Jerry Rice, whose record of 1,549 receptions may never be broken. Kelce won't catch Rice even if he plays until he's 40.

After Rice on the career catch list are Larry Fitzgerald (1,432 catches), Tony Gonzalez (1,325), Marvin Harrison (1,102), Cris Carter (1,101) and Jason Witten (1,228). Then comes Kelce, who is climbing up the ranks of the most productive pass catchers ever to play the game.

item.title: Todd Monken on Mason Graham: Hopefully we get good news
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Browns defensive tackle Mason Graham had to exit Thursday’s victory over the Steelers with a knee injury.
item.content:encoded:
Browns defensive tackle Mason Graham had to exit Thursday’s victory over the Steelers with a knee injury.

Graham was spotted postgame on crutches and wearing a brace on his knee postgame.

In his Friday news conference, Monken noted he did not have an update on Graham, who is still undergoing tests.

But Graham, the No. 5 overall pick of the 2025 draft, has been one of the team’s best players over the first few weeks of the season.

“He’s a tremendously talented young player, that you could see early in the season it all coming together,” Monken said. “Like I said last week, we want all of our young players to be great right away and we need them to be great right away. That’s the nature [of] the business we’ve chosen. But I just think he’s worked awfully hard. He’s not only active and quick, he’s a highly intelligent player — which I think helps him in terms of reading sets, in terms of communication up front, and he plays with an unbelievable effort.

“So, it’s a shame for him. But, hopefully we get good news.”

Graham has recorded 4.0 sacks with six tackles for loss and five QB hits so far in 2026. He finished last year with 0.5 sacks, seven tackles for loss, and four QB hits.

item.title: NFLPA names Mack Hollins their Community MVP for Week 4
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins has been named their Community MVP for Week 4 of the 2026 season.
item.content:encoded:
The NFL Players Association announced on Friday that Patriots wide receiver Mack Hollins has been named their Community MVP for Week 4 of the 2026 season.

Hollins recently hosted a Special Olympics Family Field Day for 125 athletes along with their families. The event featured eight different stations staffed by 25 coaches and several other Patriots players took part in the celebration,.

“It is such an honor to be named this week’s NFLPA Community MVP,” Hollins said. “I am grateful to have been able to experience it with the Special Olympics community and continue building a relationship that means so much to me. None of this would have been possible without the help of so many outstanding volunteers and passionate people.”

The NFLPA will donate $10,000 to Hollins's Free the Feet Foundation. He will also join the other weekly MVPs as candidates for the Alan Page Award at the end of the season.

item.title: Browns and Steelers mismanaged the final seconds of the game
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: On Sunday, the Ravens and the Cowboys provided stark examples on how to handle, and how not to handle, the final seconds of a close game in light of the current kickoff rules.
item.content:encoded:
On Sunday, the Ravens and the Cowboys provided stark examples on how to handle, and how not to handle, the final seconds of a close game in light of the current kickoff rules.

The Steelers and the Browns apparently learned nothing from it.

After the Browns failed to work the clock down to the final few seconds before what became the game-winning field goal, 10 seconds remained.

Like the Cowboys in Rio, the Browns kicked into the end zone, giving the Steelers the ball at the 35. (A cutaway to Browns coach Todd Monken seemed to reveal his dismay.) It opened the door for the Steelers, who had a timeout in hand, to try to gain just enough yardage to allow for a field goal that would have forced overtime.

From the TV copy, it appeared that the Browns were playing the same kind of outside leverage that the Cowboys deployed when the Ravens, who had only seven seconds to work with, gained 27 yards and kicked the walk-off field goal. That gave the Steelers a shot at completing a pass in the middle of the field.

But the Steelers didn't call a play that would have entailed a quick throw for a moderate gain and a shot at a field goal.

Instead, quarterback Aaron Rodgers rolled to his right, looking to uncork a long throw. The pass, which came back to earth just inside the Cleveland 20, was intercepted. Game over.

Why not try for a 20- to 30-yard gain? Quick decision, quick throw. If it works, take the time out and try the field goal. If it doesn't, let Rodgers try to connect on another Thursday night miracle.

Coach Mike McCarthy (or Rodgers himself) inexplicably opted for a middle ground, with a long throw that, if it had connected, possibly would have allowed for a time out and a short field goal.

The decision made no sense. The Steelers could have had two shots — a shorter attempt to put them in field goal range for overtime and, if that failed (without an interception), a Hail Mary to win it.

The 2025 shift of the touchback point from the 30 to the 35 has significantly altered the available strategies for the final 10-15 seconds of a game. The Browns repeated the Cowboys' mistake by conceding the 35, and the Steelers failed to try to seize upon the very real possibility of using the final 10 seconds to gain enough ground to send it into overtime.

item.title: T.J. Watt: Steelers made it too easy for Browns to go downfield at the end of the game
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Steelers linebacker T.J.
item.content:encoded:
Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt had a sack, two tackles for loss, a pass deflection and two quarterback hits on Thursday night, but he was not happy with the defensive effort in the 27-24 loss to the Browns.

After the Steelers tied the game 24-24 with 1:42 remaining in the fourth quarter, the Browns went 36 yards on seven plays to move into range for the game-winning field goal. Watt said that led to the Steelers losing a game they should have won.

"To sit here and not be 3-1 isn't acceptable," Watt said, via Steelers.com. "Obviously, it's a long season, a lot left to go, but we just have to put it together. Even at the end of the game, it was way too easy [for the Browns] getting down the field and getting in [field goal] range. Just have to look at everything and move forward."

The Steelers' next three games are against teams with losing records -- the Colts, Buccaneers and Saints -- and then they have a rematch with the Browns. The schedule sets up for Pittsburgh to go on a run, but Watt knows the defense needs to play better.

item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: The Jets will be shorthanded when they play the Bears on Sunday.
item.content:encoded:
The Jets will be shorthanded when they play the Bears on Sunday.

Head coach Aaron Glenn announced in his Friday press conference that Breece Hall (quad), tight end Mason Taylor (thumb), receiver Adonai Mitchell (finger), left guard Dylan Parham (knee), and linebacker Kiko Mauioga have all been ruled out.

It sounds like edge rusher Kingsley Enagbare also could end up being questionable, as Glenn said Enagbare will be a limited participant in Friday’s practice. He was limited on Wednesday but did not practice on Thursday.

Minkah Fitzpatrick appears on track to return from a groin injury, as he was upgraded to a full participant in Thursday’s practice.

New York’s full injury report with the rest of the club’s game statuses will be released later on Friday.

item.title: Drake Maye: I love playing for Mike Vrabel, that's not going to change
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel dismissed a report that he has issues with quarterback Drake Maye during a Wednesday press conference by saying that coaching Maye is the reason he's in New England and Maye got his chance to comment on it later in the day.
item.content:encoded:
Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel dismissed a report that he has issues with quarterback Drake Maye during a Wednesday press conference by saying that coaching Maye is the reason he's in New England and Maye got his chance to comment on it later in the day.

While Vrabel said he didn't "have much to add to that about a comment from an unnamed source," Maye's response avoided discussion of where the report came from and focused on how much he likes playing for the coach.

"Coach Vrabel’s been one of the best football coaches I’ve had in my life," Maye said, via a transcript from the team. "I think Coach Vrabel’s been one of the biggest things as to why this has been so enjoyable for me is playing for Coach. I think we all feel that way in the locker room. He pushes us hard. I’ve loved playing for him, and it’s not going to change. It hasn’t changed, and it won’t change. The way he pushes me, and he coaches the quarterbacks in a way that I really respect, and I’m looking forward to getting going, proving to Coach that I can lead this football team and play good football."

Maye also fielded questions about whether an injury to his shoulder is contributing to his poor play so far this season and there will continue to be questions about what's bothering a player who finished second in MVP voting last year until he starts playing at that level again.

item.title: Jayden Daniels out this week, Marcus Mariota starts again
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Daniels returned to practice this week, but he won't play against the Colts.
item.content:encoded:
Quarterback Jayden Daniels will have to wait at least one more week to return to the Commanders lineup.

Daniels was able to practice this week with a brace on his dislocated left elbow, but head coach Dan Quinn ruled him out for Sunday's game against the Colts during a Friday press conference. Marcus Mariota will get the start in London.

It's Mariota's second straight start and he was able to help the Commanders beat the Seahawks in Week 3. He was 19-of-31 for 183 yards and three touchdowns in Washington's 33-31 win.

Daniels was limited in practice this week, but a return to full participation next week would bode well for his chances of playing against the Giants in Week 5.

While Daniels will remain out, Quinn said linebacker Frankie Luvu and tight end Chig Okonkwo will play against Indianapolis. Both players missed the last two games.

item.title: Roger Goodell met with Gov. JB Pritzker, Illinois lawmakers about Bears stadium on Thursday
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: Publicly, the Bears have said their "sole focus" for the site of their new stadium site is Hammond, Ind.
item.content:encoded:
Publicly, the Bears have said their "sole focus" for the site of their new stadium site is Hammond, Ind.

But the storied franchise playing its home games in a different state is not a done deal — potentially far from it.

After there was reporting in August that commissioner Roger Goodell had met with select state lawmakers, Illinois Governor JB Pritzker issued a statement on Thursday saying he had met with Goodell.

"The Governor's Office has remained in conversation with the Bears about their plans in Illinois throughout the summer,” the statement reads. "Today, Governor Pritzker was grateful to meet in Illinois with NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell, Pat Ryan, Speaker Emanuel "Chris" Welch, Rep. Kam Buckner, and Sen. Bill Cunningham.

"The Governor and General Assembly leadership were glad to participate in a productive meeting focused on keeping the Bears in Illinois and protecting taxpayers."

Ryan is a Bears minority owner, and the namesake of Northwestern University’s Ryan Field, which was recently rebuilt and is set to open on Friday when the Wildcats play Penn State.

Interestingly, none of speaker Welch, Rep. Buckner, or Sen. Cunningham represent Arlington Heights — which is the suburb of Chicago where the Bears purchased a 326-acre property for a new stadium and development. But all three do represent districts in and around Chicago.

The league also issued a statement on the meeting, via Ian Rapoport of NFL Network:

“The NFL appreciated the opportunity to meet with Governor Pritzker and legislative leaders today,” the statement reads. “Timely action is essential as the Bears work to find a long-term stadium solution for the club and their fans.”

It’s unclear what the solution will be for the Bears and their stadium going forward. But it does appear that at least the league is working to keep the club playing its home games in its home state.

item.title: Mike McCarthy doesn't know whether the Joey Porter Jr. trade affected the team
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Steelers traded cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys less than 24 hours before their Week 4 game at Cleveland.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers traded cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys less than 24 hours before their Week 4 game at Cleveland. After the 27-24 loss, coach Mike McCarthy was asked whether the timing of the move had a negative impact on the team.

"You know, I mean, that's really, you know, a question that's really specific to individuals, and I can't really speak on every individual," McCarthy said. "You know, the timing was, you know, was the night before a game, and, you know, I'm sure that's what the guys woke up to but, yeah, I mean, it's part of our business."

Earlier in the press conference, McCarthy revisited the intersection between business and football, as it played out throughout the Porter saga.

"You never hope business, you know, gets in the way of your preparation and playing, but, you know, it's the modern NFL," McCarthy said. "You know, it was a situation where, you know, it's been going on for some time. As an organization, we felt like this was the best thing for us and, you know, we wish Joey well, and, you know, I never really got a chance to coach Joey, but, you know, obviously, did some, you know, did some great things here, and we wish him the best in Dallas."

McCarthy added that there "was definitely a point" where he "definitely thought it was a possibility" that Porter would play for the Steelers against the Browns.

"We had a rep count in mind," McCarthy said, "so that's what we were working towards."

Quarterback Aaron Rodgers also got a question about the timing of the Porter trade and the potential impact on the team.

"You gotta ask the defensive guys," Rodgers said. "They're probably around him more often but, you know, I thought Joey might play this week, based on his practice stuff but, you know, we wish Joey well."

One defensive player wasn't surprised by the move. At the outset of the Thursday night broadcast, Kaylee Hartung said linebacker Patrick Queen knew that, when Porter didn't get on the bus with the team to Cleveland, "he wouldn't be in Pittsburgh when they came back."

Porter is now in Dallas. And it appears that he will indeed make his 2026 debut on Sunday, when the Cowboys face the Texans.

item.title: Jalen Ramsey on Joey Porter Jr.: Unfortunate it didn't work out, but I'm happy for him
item.dc:creator: Myles Simmons
item.description: After a long, drawn out negotiation, the Steelers dealt cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys on Wednesday night.
item.content:encoded:
After a long, drawn out negotiation, the Steelers dealt cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Cowboys on Wednesday night.

Porter's now-former teammate Jalen Ramsey went through a similar situation with the Jaguars back in 2019, which ended with him being traded to the Rams.

After Thursday night's loss to the Rams, Ramsey told reporters that he felt like a big brother to Porter and wanted him to be a valued, important part of the Steelers going forward.

“It is very unfortunate that it didn’t work out,” Ramsey said, via Mark Kaboly of the Pat McAfee Show. “But at the same time, I am happy for him. I am happy that he is getting a fresh start. I wish him all the success in his NFL future. I think he is a stud, I really do. I think he is a top-five guy. People argue that he’s top 10, but I really think Joey is a good player, I really do.”

Ramsey also referenced his own story and compared it to Porter.

“It happens, and everybody moves on,” Ramsey said. “For me, I’ve been through it before. I was Joey before at one point. When I was 24, I was Joey. A little different; our situations were a little bit different. The exit was similar, potentially. It is what it is. I treat it as part of the NFL business. We held hope as long as we could that things would get done, but that’s part of it. That’s business. Guys have to do what’s best for them because the NFL is not for long. You have to do what is best for you, and you can’t be mad at a man wanting to do that.”

item.title: Mike McDaniel: I'm not living in hope, I'm living in reality about our offense
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel got a vote of confidence from head coach Jim Harbaugh on Wednesday, but he knows that the status quo on offense isn't going to work.
item.content:encoded:
Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel got a vote of confidence from head coach Jim Harbaugh on Wednesday, but he knows that the status quo on offense isn't going to work.

The Chargers lost to the Bills last Sunday despite being plus-four in the turnover column and McDaniel said at a Thursday press conference that "we were the reason we lost a football game." They had five turnovers over the first two games, so the unit had a big hand in those losses as well.

McDaniel said he hasn't lost faith in the offense and thinks he has "a much better understanding" of what can bring out better play in quarterback Justin Herbert, but he acknowledged that results on the field are the only thing that matter.

"There has been improvement, but does anyone care? No, but we better improve. . . . I’m not trying to have moral victories or anything like that," McDaniel said. "It’s steadfast that there’s things that we’ve done in the past three games that is active participation in losing the game. Flat out, our jobs are to improve everything. I’m not living in hope, I’m living in reality."

It won't be the easiest week to get on track as the Chargers will be in Seattle to face the Seahawks they try to bounce back from the end of their 12-game losing streak. McDaniel and the Chargers need to find a way, however, or the next vote of confidence may never come.

item.title: Report: "Final straw" for Steelers was Joey Porter Jr.'s Wednesday claim of back pain
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: The Steelers thought the dance was over.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers thought the dance was over. When the music started up again, they decided they'd had enough.

As explained by Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette, the "final straw" for the Steelers in their relationship with cornerback Joey Porter Jr. came when Porter, after two days of fully participating in practice, claimed that he had back pain on Wednesday.

That's when the Steelers decided to make a trade.

Ultimately, it was a win for Porter. He got what he wanted — a one-way ticket out of town.

Former Cowboys linebacker Micah Parsons achieved the same result last year. Once the Cowboys realized he was serious about not playing unless and until he got a new deal, they traded him to the Packers. For the Steelers, who seemed to think Porter eventually would blink, the fourth game became the moment they accepted that Porter was committed to the bit.

And, yes, it was a bit. He wasn't too injured to play, if he was injured at all. Amazingly, he's not even listed on the Cowboys' injury report, one day after being limited on Pittsburgh's final report of the week, and in turn ruled out for Thursday night's game.

For players who can't hold out due to the financial consequences under the Collective Bargaining Agreement, a hold in that lingers until they get what they want is the best, and only, alternative.

Was it a real injury? If the team has no way to challenge it without creating an ugly legal fight and/or a P.R. shitstorm, it doesn't matter.

For most players, a lifetime of football has caused some condition from the top of their head to the tips of their toes that would justify not playing. Unless the team is willing to stage a confrontation that would instantly ruin an already tenuous relationship, the only viable option is to trade the player.

item.title: Joey Porter Jr.'s back is "feeling better," and he hopes to play Sunday
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Steelers had ruled out the cornerback for Thursday Night Football.
item.content:encoded:
The Cowboys' injury report did not change Thursday. The only thing that changed was the trade for cornerback Joey Porter Jr., who was not listed on the report.

That was news in and of itself from the report as Porter practiced after passing his physical.

The Steelers had ruled out Porter for Thursday night's game against the Browns, adding his on-again, off-again back issue on Wednesday's injury report.

In no surprise, Porter said his back was "feeling better" after the trade to the Cowboys.

He hopes to make his 2026 debut on Sunday when the Cowboys play the Texans.

"We're just trying to take things day by day," Porter said after his first practice in Dallas, via Todd Archer of ESPN, "and if everything looks good, then we should be out there."

Porter's addition gives the team depth at the position, with cornerbacks Shavon Revel (right knee/right ankle) and Cobie Durant (hamstring) still not practicing.

Porter did not get the contract extension he wanted in Pittsburgh and was holding in, an inactive for the first three games. He will play in Dallas on the final year of his deal, because, he said, the Cowboys have shown him "value" that the Steelers didn't.

“I think he’s excited about the opportunity to maybe play, but we’ll see how the rest of the week goes," Cowboys coach Brian Schottenheimer said, via Joseph Hoyt of the Dallas Morning News. "This was a good start today.”

Porter said he got what he wanted in going to the Cowboys and now he would like to finish his career in Dallas.

"I'm down with it if they are. I want to finish my career here," Porter said. "So hopefully I just perform like how I know how to perform and do what I do, and I'm going to let everything take care of the rest."

Linebacker DeMarvion Overshown (hamstring) also did not practice a second consecutive day, and safety Malik Hooker (fractured forearm) was limited again after returning to practice Wednesday.

Outside linebacker James Houston (shoulder) remained a full participant.

item.title: Deshaun Watson: Momentum shifts are part of the NFL, you have to ride the waves
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: When Thursday night's game got to halftime, it looked like the Browns might roll over the Steelers for an easy win.
item.content:encoded:
When Thursday night's game got to halftime, it looked like the Browns might roll over the Steelers for an easy win.

After going scoreless in the first quarter, Cleveland found the end zone on three straight possessions in the second quarter and carried a 21-10 win into halftime. Things went south again after the break, however, and a Deshaun Watson interception helped spark a 14-3 Steelers run in the fourth quarter that put overtime on the table.

Watson and the Browns had been in similar straits in their last two games and they came through for the third straight week. Watson completed four passes for 45 yards and the Browns survived a late sack and incompletion when Andre Szymt hit a 56-yard field goal for a 27-24 win.

“That’s part of the NFL. You have to ride the waves," Watson said, via a transcript from the team. "So many momentum shifts, they are the best in the world, just like us. They are a really good team. They are going to make plays, and they made a couple of plays that went their way. We made a couple of plays that went our way. We just have to ride the wave until our opportunities came and at the end of the day, whenever those moments come, especially at the end, we found a way to get the W. That’s what ultimately matters.”

Watson's feelings about riding the waves was about Thursday night, but it's something that can be applied to his entire run in Cleveland. For much of that time, it looked like a shipwreck was the only possible outcome, but the last few weeks have offered long-awaited reasons to believe otherwise.

item.title: Aaron Rodgers' second TD draws Steelers to within 21-16
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: The Steelers had minus-6 yards passing in the third quarter as the Browns had two sacks of Aaron Rodgers.
item.content:encoded:
The Steelers had minus-6 yards passing in the third quarter as the Browns had two sacks of Aaron Rodgers.

The fourth quarter has gotten off to a better start for the visitors.

On the second play of the final quarter, the Steelers had a pass interference penalty overturned on replay. Robert Spears-Jennings intercepted Deshaun Waston's deep pass intended for Denzel Boston.

Steelers defensive back Daylen Everette was called for defensive pass interference, though, and the 42-yard penalty had the Browns at the Pittsburgh 23. The Steelers challenged the play, and it was reversed on replay because Jack Sawyer tipped the pass at the line of scrimmage, negating the penalty.

Rodgers took advantage with a six-play, 77-yard touchdown drive.

He rolled to his right to avoid another sack and threw a 21-yard touchdown pass to tight end Darnell Washington. The Browns stopped the 2-point conversion, leaving the Steelers trailing 21-16.

Rodgers is 16-of-29 for 222 yards with two touchdowns and an interception.

item.title: Thursday Night Football: Deshaun Watson leads Browns to 27-24 win over Steelers
item.dc:creator: Charean Williams
item.description: Watson drove the Browns 36 yards in seven plays to set up Andre Szmyt's 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left.
item.content:encoded:
The Browns is the Browns? Forget that.

Cleveland upset Pittsburgh 27-24 on Thursday Night Football, moving into sole possession of first place in the AFC North if only briefly. The Browns are 3-1, a half-game better than the Bengals and Ravens, while the Steelers are 2-2.

Browns kicker Andre Szmyt kicked a 56-yard field goal with 10 seconds left for the game-winner in an entertaining game.

Aaron Rodgers had the ball at the 35 after the Browns kicked it into the end zone, but safety Grant Delpit intercepted Rodgers at the Cleveland 18.

Deshaun Watson played a flawless first half, with 181 yards and a touchdown, before the Steelers adjusted in the second half. The Browns quarterback finished 24-of-33 for 268 yards with a touchdown and an interception. Both of his turnovers came in the second half, with his interception changing the momentum.

On the second play of the final quarter, the Steelers had a pass interference penalty overturned on replay and reversed to an interception.

Robert Spears-Jennings intercepted Watson’s deep pass intended for Denzel Boston. Steelers defensive back Daylen Everette was called for defensive pass interference, though, and the 42-yard penalty had the Browns at the Pittsburgh 23. The Steelers challenged the play, and it was reversed on replay because Jack Sawyer tipped the pass at the line of scrimmage, negating the penalty.

It led to Rodgers' second touchdown pass, a 21-yarder to tight end Darnell Washington, that drew the Steelers to within 21-16 after a failed 2-point conversion.

After Szmyt's 44-yard field goal, Rodgers drove the Steelers to a late tie.

The Steelers faced a fourth-and-10 at the Cleveland 11 with 1:51 remaining. Rodgers targeted Washington for a third consecutive play, and safety Emmanuel McNeil-Warren was penalized for pass interference. Rodgers then hit Pat Freiermuth for a 3-yard touchdown on the next play, with 1:42 left. Rodgers tied it with a quarterback sneak on the 2-point conversion from the 1-yard line after Jared Verse jumped offsides.

The Steelers, though, couldn't stop the Browns, who drove 36 yards in seven plays for the winning field goal.

Cleveland finished with 372 yards and the Steelers 361.

Rodgers went 22-of-40 for 299 yards with three touchdowns and two interceptions. Jaylen Warren rushed for 93 yards on 17 carries, and DK Metcalf caught five passes for 115 yards. Roman Wilson added three catches for 74 yards.

The Browns sacked Rodgers five times, but they had to overcome 14 penalties for 88 yards.

item.title: Signs point to Tyson Bagent for the Bears on Sunday
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: As Bears coach Ben Johnson prepares for a reunion with fellow former Lions coordinator Aaron Glenn, Johnson is doing his best to keep Glenn and the Jets in the dark about who the starting quarterback will be.
item.content:encoded:
As Bears coach Ben Johnson prepares for a reunion with fellow former Lions coordinator Aaron Glenn, Johnson is doing his best to keep Glenn and the Jets in the dark about who the starting quarterback will be.

It's one of the benefits of having injury issues complicate the most important position in pro football. The uncertainty can be weaponized, in the hopes of preventing the next opponent from knowing who they'll face.

Johnson is trying his damnedest to keep the plans for Week 4 secret. Through two full practice days in advance of the game against the Jets, he has largely succeeded.

That said, it's hard to keep the many people who are present for practice from saying something to someone who is trying to find out who's getting the work. As we hear it, Tyson Bagent (not Case Keenum) has gotten the first-team reps so far this week.

This obviously points to Bagent as the starter in place of Caleb Williams, who continues to recover from a hamstring injury.

It makes sense. Bagent earned the backup role. He entered the Week 2 game against the Vikings in the fourth quarter and nearly pulled off a last-second win.

Keenum got the Monday night start because he was available to prepare for the game against the Eagles at a time when Bagent was in the concussion protocol. By the time Bagent was cleared, the hay was in the barn with Keenum.

The question of whether a coach can keep the identity of his starting quarterback a secret is separate from whether the league should allow it. It creates another chunk of inside information that could be mishandled by those who know the truth.

Presumably, the Bears will make an announcement today. Or maybe they won't. The rules don't require it.

And if it's Bagent, the Bears can say they necessarily made the announcement by not updating their depth chart. Bagent is No. 2, Keenum is No. 3. Both are healthy. Common sense points to Bagent.

If he's indeed getting all of the practice reps, that only reinforces it.

item.title: Mike McCarthy on exchange with Aaron Rodgers: "I wish I wouldn't use those words"
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: In the first quarter of Thursday night's game between the Steelers and the Browns, Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers became upset.
item.content:encoded:
In the first quarter of Thursday night's game between the Steelers and the Browns, Pittsburgh quarterback Aaron Rodgers became upset.

Given that he's often upset during games, that doesn't really narrow it down.

He was particularly perturbed that the play was coming in too slowly. And a microphone caught his words.

"What the fuck?" Rodgers angrily said to the sideline. "Call it."

The Prime Video cameras then cut to coach Mike McCarthy, who seemed to say, "Fucking asshole."

After the game, McCarthy initially feigned confusion when asked about communication issues. When the questioning became more specific, he said that Steelers P.R. director Burt Lauten had told McCarthy about the exchange that made its way to TV.

"Communication sometimes is not the best choice of words, but everybody's competing on the field," McCarthy said. "I think, you know, what's said on the field, the way I grew up in this game, you know, usually stays on the field. That's not the case today. I understand that. But, yeah, any negative communication on my part, I wish I wouldn't use those words."

For Rodgers's part, he wasn't asked about the specific exchange.

Either way, the Steelers fell to 2-2. They're currently in last place in the AFC North, as the only team with two losses. If the Bengals and Ravens win on Sunday, the Steelers will be all alone in the basement of the division.

item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was traded to the Cowboys late on Wednesday night and went through his first practice with the team on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
Cornerback Joey Porter Jr. was traded to the Cowboys late on Wednesday night and went through his first practice with the team on Thursday.

Porter did not practice all summer because of what was called a back injury and had been on the injury report in Pittsburgh during the season due to that injury or conditioning needs related to his long absence. He was not on the Cowboys' injury report for any reason, which has led to thoughts that he will be on the field for Dallas when they face the Texans on Sunday.

During a Friday appearance on 105.3 The Fan, Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer said the team is still working out whether Porter will make his debut this weekend.

“We’ll see how he moves around today, see if he’s sore today," Schottenheimer said, via Jon Machota of TheAthletic.com. "But I thought it was a great start yesterday. Really, really pleased with not just what I saw on the field, but really just the way he attacked his preparation and in learning the system. The big thing that will drive this is his ability to communicate with Caleb Downs and some of the safeties and things like that as we get ready to finish the prep.”

Schottenheimer called the deal for Porter a sign the Cowboys are in "win-now mode" and that suggests we'll be seeing the newest Cowboy on the field sooner rather than later.

item.title: Falcons announce death of Ring of Honor member Jeff Van Note
item.dc:creator: Josh Alper
item.description: The Falcons announced on Friday that their longtime center Jeff Van Note has died at the age of 80.
item.content:encoded:
The Falcons announced on Friday that their longtime center Jeff Van Note has died at the age of 80.

Van Note was selected by the Falcons in the 11th round of the 1969 draft and he remained with the team through the 1986 season. Van Note was added to the franchise Ring of Honor in 2006

Van Note played linebacker at Alabama, but was moved to center by then-Falcons head coach Norm Van Brocklin. He became a starter in 1970 and was named a second-team All-Pro twice while making six Pro Bowls.

"Today, we mourn the loss of a true Falcons legend," Falcons owner Arthur Blank said in a statement. "Jeff Van Note dedicated 18 seasons to this franchise and became one of the most respected and beloved players in our history. He embodied toughness, resilience, humility, and an unwavering commitment to his team, qualities that earned him the admiration of generations of Falcons fans."

Van Note played in 246 games during his time with the Falcons, which is second only to his former teammate Mike Kenn in franchise history.

item.title: Darren Rizzi: Special teams coaches want NFL to change rule for holders on kickoffs
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Broncos special teams coach Darren Rizzi says his colleagues around the league almost all agree that holders should be allowed on kickoffs only if the wind is blowing the ball off the tee, and not to give the kicking team an advantage by placing the ball at an unusual angle.
item.content:encoded:
Broncos special teams coach Darren Rizzi says his colleagues around the league almost all agree that holders should be allowed on kickoffs only if the wind is blowing the ball off the tee, and not to give the kicking team an advantage by placing the ball at an unusual angle.

Under the NFL's dynamic kickoff rule, a 12th player can take the field as a holder on kickoffs, with our without the use of a tee, as long as the holder runs off the field immediately after the ball is kicked. Rizzi says the intent of the rule was to allow the kicking team to ensure the ball would stay in the tee on windy days, but the Eagles gained attention in Week 2 for using a holder just to hold the ball on the ground at an odd angle, which changes the trajectory of the kick and makes it harder to return.

Rizzi helped organize a conference call of special teams coordinators and said almost everyone agreed that the NFL should change the way the rule is officiated so that kickoffs are on a tee and holders are for weather conditions, not creating an advantage for the kicker.

“We don’t want the ball on the edge, we don’t want the ball on the ground, we don’t want the ball held sideways. We want just a regular kickoff,” Rizzi said. “That's kind of what was discussed amongst the coordinators. If we’re not unanimous, we’re darn close to it, the way we feel about it. That's why you saw some holders come out to start the game. And that's really not the intent. It's a work in progress. It hasn't been remedied yet."

Rizzi said there's no question the kicking team benefits from using the holder.

"There's definitely an advantage from the kicker's standpoint because the different angles you can create with the ball," Rizzi said. "That's fine if you want to kick one of those knuckleballs or dirty balls with the ball in a tee, have at it. Adding the 12th player to create an advantage is something we want to stay away from."

The rules allow for the holder, but Rizzi would like to see an administrative change similar to the one the NFL made during the 2022 season, when the Raiders were told they had to stop using a holder to place the football on top of the tee, rather than in the tee. Rizzi said he believes the NFL will do that.

"It's a small little thing that created a big problem." Rizzi said. "I think we're gonna get it resolved."

item.title: Denzel Ward: I hope Aaron Rodgers keeps throwing at me
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Ward intercepted Rodgers on Thursday night in the Browns' 27-24 win.
item.content:encoded:
Browns cornerback Denzel Ward intercepted Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers in the second quarter of the Browns' 27-24 win on Thursday night, and he said after the game that he loves it when Rodgers throws at him.

Asked if Rodgers will stop throwing at him after Thursday night's game, Ward answered, "I hope not. I hope he keeps throwing at me. Good things happen when he throws at me. I hope he keeps throwing at me."

At the time of Ward's interception, the Steelers were winning 7-0 with 14 minutes left in the second quarter. By the time there was 1 minute left in the second quarter, the Browns were winning 21-7. Browns coach Todd Monken made a point of mentioning Ward's interception as the play that turned the game around.

"Big credit to Denzel Ward. He changed the momentum of the game. We just didn't convert the first drive, and then we had a big play and stalled, and then Denzel flipped it and we go things going," Monken said.

Ward said he thinks the Browns are turning things around.

"It felt good. It just shows the resilience of this team, this organization, and all the fans. It's been a lot of up and downs, but we're on a winning track right now, changing the organization right now, and we're looking to stack one on top of the other," Ward said on the Prime Video broadcast.

How many more wins the Browns can stack remains to be seen, but right now they're 3-1 and atop the AFC North.

item.title: Tom Brady thinks the Raiders are a Top 5 team in the NFL right now
item.dc:creator: Michael David Smith
item.description: Raiders minority owner Tom Brady believes the Raiders are one of the five best teams in the NFL.
item.content:encoded:
Raiders minority owner Tom Brady believes the Raiders are one of the five best teams in the NFL.

Wearing his other hat as a Fox commentator, Brady released power rankings that put the Raiders at No. 5. Brady said the Raiders have earned it, as one of the NFL's five unbeaten teams.

"No hometown bias here: The Las Vegas Raiders. Undefeated gets you in the Top 5," Brady said. "That's just the way my power rankings work. You can only beat who you play, and when you're undefeated you're better than the teams that lost games. That's just the way it works for me."

But Brady said it's about more than just the Raiders' record. He believe they're creating a winning culture.

"I think it's always about your teammates, it's about 'we' over 'me,' you go out there and you play for your teammates every single game. You try not to let your teammates down. I love the way the culture is being built in Las Vegas right now," Brady said.

The four teams Brady ranks ahead of the Raiders are the 49ers first, Chiefs second, Bills third and Vikings fourth.

item.title: Nick Saban says he was offered Giants job in 1997
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Nick Saban's two-year stint as an NFL head coach began in 2005.
item.content:encoded:
Nick Saban's two-year stint as an NFL head coach began in 2005. It could have started eight years earlier.

In a Thursday interview with Chris "Mad Dog" Russo of SiriusXM Mad Dog Radio, Saban admitted — eventually — that the Giants had offered him the head-coaching job after the Giants fired Dan Reeves, when Saban was the head coach at Michigan State.

"It's very difficult in college, you know, and the NFL, you have an opportunity to go to the NFL, you're still coaching, you're still recruiting," Saban said. "If you stay in college, you don't want it to upset your coaching and recruiting and all that. So you don't wanna say that I'm gonna go interview for the Giants job. So [G.M.] George [Young] and I worked out a deal. He said, 'Well, where do you think we can meet and nobody would know it?' And I said, 'The least obvious place you would ever think. Just come to my house in East Lansing and nobody will ever know it.' That's what he did."

In other words, Saban (like plenty of other college coaches over the years) had made various promises that he didn't want anyone to know he was thinking about breaking, until the moment he decided to do so.

So did the Giants offer him the job in 1997?

"You know, I can't really remember what we talked about and how we ended up there, but I think Ernie [Accorsi] was assistant general manager then," Saban said. "And I love Ernie. He was at the Browns when I was there with Belichick. Yeah, they did offer me the job actually."

Saban obviously didn't take it. The Giants hired Jim Fassel, who took them to the Super Bowl in 2000.

It's unclear whether the Giants made another run at Saban after Fassel was fired, after the 2003 season. A year later, Saban took the Dolphins job.

If he'd jumped to the NFL in 1997, Saban would have faced the same issues he did in Miami. The salary cap is the great equalizer, and there's no way to recruit an annual flock of players who are the equivalent of NFL first-round picks. Saban learned that, at the college level, it's a lot easier to stack the deck in his favor.

item.title: Puka Nacua is "taking it one day at a time" in his return from hip injury
item.dc:creator: Mike Florio
item.description: Rams receiver Puka Nacua has missed the last two games with a hip injury.
item.content:encoded:
Rams receiver Puka Nacua has missed the last two games with a hip injury. He's moving closer to a return.

“I'm taking it one day at a time, but I felt great being out there, full practice today for the first time," Nacua told reporters on Thursday. "I'm getting my feet under me, hearing all the play calls. It's not as foreign as it used to sound from Matthew Stafford, but he's definitely in full flow and rhythm. It's nice to be able to hear that play call in the huddle. I have to make sure I buckle my stuff up before so I can really focus on what he's saying.”

Nacua said twice on Thursday that he fully participated in practice; officially, he was listed as limited.

He first noticed the problem a couple of weeks ago at practice.

“Just in some of the change of direction stuff, some of the stuff in my hip area just was not feeling great," Nacua said. "It was causing me some pain and some restriction in some of my movements. I was trying to grind through it, but definitely some sharp pains that I started to feel that put me down.”

Now, he's able to do what he used to do.

“One hundred percent," Nacua said. "I've been working through it like getting acceleration, change of direction. Today being a full participant in practice, I was definitely able to work through some of the rustiness.”

It's been described by the Rams as a hip problem. It's been referred to elsewhere as a groin injury. It's basically both.

“The hip area, this right side on the front side of the hip and groin," Nacua said. "I was feeling it really in that hip. Then with all the connection, understanding . . . everything in this hip area being tied down to all parts of everything, core and change of direction and things like that so really on the right hip-groin area.”

Whatever the specific problem, it seems to be resolving itself. And the Rams could use the boost that would come from Nacua's presence on the field on Sunday at the Eagles.
